faq: Does this work with the old shortcode checkout?
We build for the block checkout first, as it is now the default. If your store still uses the shortcode checkout, tell us and we add fields for it too, which may need extra time.
Will it work with my payment plugin?
Usually yes, if the payment plugin supports the block checkout. We test with your payment method on a staging copy and tell you if the plugin itself lacks block support.
Can fields show only for some products?
Yes. Standard and Premium support conditions such as a field that appears only when a given product, category or shipping method is in the cart.
Do you need access to my live checkout?
No. We build and test on a staging copy. You review it there, and we install it on the live store only when you approve, using an administrator user you add for us.
desc:
WooCommerce block checkout customization means adding fields, notes and custom blocks that work in the current block-based checkout instead of breaking it. Ecom Swift LLC builds them so the data saves to the order, shows in admin and reaches your order emails.

## What is WooCommerce block checkout customization?

It is the work of adding or changing checkout content in the block-based Cart and Checkout, using the extension points WooCommerce provides for it. Examples are a delivery instruction field, a gift message, a company tax reference, or a custom block that shows a notice next to the order summary.

The block checkout is built differently from the older shortcode checkout. Code that hooked into the old template often does nothing in the new one. That is why a field that used to work can quietly vanish after a store switches.

## Why do older checkout field plugins stop working?

Older plugins add fields by printing HTML through PHP hooks that the shortcode checkout runs. The block checkout renders in the browser from JavaScript components and talks to the store through its own API. Hooks written for the old page are never called, so the field never appears or never saves.

The result is easy to miss. The checkout still loads and still takes payment, but the information you needed from the customer is gone. Staff find out later, when an order arrives without the delivery note or the VAT number it was supposed to carry.

## How checkout fields affect completed orders

Every extra question at checkout has a cost, so each field should earn its place. A field that collects information you truly need, such as a delivery window or a purchase order number, prevents follow-up emails and wrong shipments. A field that nobody reads only adds friction.

Clear labels and plain error messages matter just as much. If a required field fails with a vague message, shoppers abandon the form. If the message says exactly what to fix, they correct it and continue. Good validation protects both the customer's time and your data quality.

## What a well-built block checkout customization includes

- Fields registered through WooCommerce's current additional checkout field support, not through old template hooks.
- Required or optional behavior chosen field by field.
- Field values saved to the order and visible on the order edit screen in admin.
- Values included in the order emails your team and customers receive.
- Validation with specific, polite error messages.
- Conditional display, so a field appears only for the products or shipping methods that need it.
- Custom blocks for the editor that follow your theme styling.
- Fields saved on the customer account when returning shoppers should not retype them.
- Order exports that include the new data.
- A test pass in the block checkout on desktop and phone.

## What we do

We start by confirming which checkout you use, the block-based one or the shortcode one, and which fields you need. We write down each field's label, type, rules and where its value should appear. Nothing is built until that list is agreed.

We then build on a staging copy of your store. We register the fields, connect them to the order, add the admin display and email output, and write the validation messages. Where your package includes custom blocks, we build them for the block editor and check them on a real page. We place test orders with your active payment and shipping plugins to confirm nothing conflicts. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many fields and blocks they cover and how much testing and data handling is included.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Ask only for information you will actually use.
- Mark a field as required only when an order cannot be fulfilled without it.
- Write error messages that say what to change.
- Test with your real payment methods, not only the default one.
- Keep a staging copy so changes are checked before shoppers see them.

**Avoid:**
- Installing a second plugin that rewrites the checkout page.
- Adding long forms that make shoppers feel they are applying for something.
- Hiding important notes in small gray text.
- Editing the checkout template files directly, which the block checkout ignores.
- Skipping a phone test, since many shoppers pay from a phone.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a store owner whose old checkout field plugin stopped showing fields after moving to the block checkout. It suits a wholesale or business-to-business seller who needs tax numbers or purchase references on every order. It also suits a shop that delivers locally and wants a date, a time window or access instructions captured cleanly.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of each field you want, which products or shipping methods it applies to, and where your team needs to see it. Tell us which payment and shipping plugins you use. We never ask for passwords. Please add us as a collaborator or staff user, or give us a staging copy to work on, and we will confirm the setup in a short checklist.
